# Grounded project verification and acceptance

- Status: Draft
- Date: 2026-11-04
- Catalog capability ID: fixture-foundation (companion specification; not a new owner)
- Last verified: not applicable; this is a prospective qualification document
- Owners: Fixture maintainer; maintainer owns acceptance
- Scope: Define 18 bounded protocol refinements and planned evidence for the existing fixture-foundation capability without changing implementation or runtime policy.
- Related issues/PRs: [Issue #47](https://github.com/owned/fixture/issues/47)
- Required review gates: product UX, architecture, testing, documentation, security/operations
- Open decisions blocking readiness: Concrete product implementation, consumer execution support, and invocation of any future acceptance harness remain unverified; this authored qualification request does not establish them.

> Draft for review. Catalog ownership remains with `fixture-foundation` and [specs/foundation.md](foundation.md). This companion does not replace that owner or its three retained baseline cases.

## 1. Executive summary

Maintainers need a precise, reviewable set of expected outcomes for grounded project verification. This companion defines 18 distinct protocol refinements, retaining the authentication baseline owned by [specs/foundation.md](foundation.md). Each refinement is a future acceptance scenario, not evidence of implemented or executed behavior. The recommended default is to preserve independently verified progress and reject stale, unauthorized, duplicated, or mismatched transitions. No runtime permission, installation, source implementation, or compatibility policy changes are authorized or specified.

```text
Maintainer reviews this Draft -> future implementation supplies evidence -> maintainer evaluates each observable case -> accepted contract remains alongside the foundation baseline
```

## 2. Problem, current behavior, and evidence

### 2.1 Problem

The fixture maintainer needs grounded, concrete assertions to qualify correctness across recovery, generation boundaries, cursors, checkpoints, clocks, acknowledgments, authorization, and concurrency. A broad statement such as “preserve progress” would not reveal which independent failure modes were checked. The 18 supplied cases make those expected outcomes reviewable without implying that a consumer implementation exists.

### 2.2 Current behavior

1. The selected catalog records `fixture-foundation` as implemented, with specification `specs/foundation.md`, entrypoint and code `app/core.py`, test evidence `checks/test_core.py`, and documentation `docs/payments.mdx`; its workflow list is empty. These are catalog facts, not proof that the files implement the requested protocol behavior.
2. The selected source `app/core.py` defines `identity(value)` returning its input. `checks/test_core.py` contains one assertion that `identity(1) == 1`. Neither establishes any of the 18 requested behaviors.
3. `specs/foundation.md` is Draft and owns the retained authentication cases `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03`. Those remain required and are not counted or redefined here.
4. This companion is a proposed authored qualification request. Its cases are planned acceptance only. No source, execution, or compatibility change is proposed.

### 2.3 Evidence

- Code/workflow/documentation references: `app/core.py`; `checks/test_core.py`; `specs/foundation.md`; `specs/catalog.json`; `specs/CATALOG.md`; `docs/payments.mdx`; `docs/commands.md`; `package.json`. The selected owner identity is recorded in `docs/source-evidence.md`: Git blob `16f39aed096aae5cd8dee237d607ae606e802d2e`, SHA-256 `7edf1cb9ad46f8c06db97ecef6c8ddb4bc06bcb2a7793a1f4c6c8533a205ad60` for `specs/foundation.md`.
- Incidents or concrete examples: No incident evidence supplied. The 18 protocol cases below are authored prospective examples, not observed failures.
- External primary sources: Issue #47 is the request context; it is not implementation evidence.
- Unknowns: Whether a target runtime, state store, test harness, or consumer documentation supports these protocols; concrete execution commands; any underlying schema, provider, or deployment behavior.

### 2.4 Retrospective classification (as-built baselines only)

Not applicable: this prospective companion does not reconstruct an implemented baseline. Current facts are limited to the cited selected source files and catalog metadata; proposed outcomes are not current behavior.

## 3. Actors, surfaces, and terminology

| Actor | Goal | Entry point | Visible surfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixture maintainer | Review and accept grounded assertions | Issue #47 and this Draft | Issue, specification, future evidence artifacts |
| Future implementer | Provide evidence for each accepted behavior | Future reviewed implementation work | Source, tests, documentation, review |
| Future operator | Understand retained versus rejected progress | Future product surface, if one exists | Exact product surface remains unverified |

A **generation** is a protocol-defined scan lifecycle; its concrete representation is unspecified. A **checkpoint** is persisted recovery evidence. A **cursor** identifies outstanding continuation work. A **journal** is an independently recoverable progress stream. A **lease** gates writer authority. A **local day** is the calendar day interpreted by the request’s configured locality. A **case** is one distinct planned observable assertion. The maintainer owns acceptance decisions; this document owns only these proposed qualification statements. No branch naming, storage schema, product UI, or concrete runtime surface is established by the source evidence.

## 4. Goals

### 4.1 Goals

| Requirement | Behavior |
|---|---|
| G-01 | On checkpoint restore without bootstrap state, create no initial work silently; the next explicit bootstrap records exactly one generation. |
| G-02 | A full final source-scan chunk with lookahead consisting only of seen records closes at the exact unique-record boundary, with no empty extra cycle. |
| G-03 | A completion token from a previous generation cannot complete or reopen the current generation. |
| G-04 | Independent journals may share a high revision; resuming one cannot consume the other journal’s checkpoint. |
| G-05 | If persisted storage version is genuinely nine and a late migration fails, roll back every new record and retain version nine. |
| G-06 | Include an item at the exact configured stop instant once and defer the immediately later item. |
| G-07 | Canceling an active cursor prevents its later response from appending work to a replacement cursor. |
| G-08 | Replaying an accepted continuation key returns its prior batch without incrementing counters. |
| G-09 | An expired writer cannot commit the final batch; the new lease holder retains its independently accepted progress. |
| G-10 | Mismatched-checkpoint recovery refuses that checkpoint and preserves the last independently verified checkpoint. |
| G-11 | A backward wall-clock adjustment after resume does not renew the monotonic deadline. |
| G-12 | A completed empty scan advances the explicit generation once and preserves its no-work reason. |
| G-13 | Restart preserves pending acknowledged journal entries and does not count them as newly generated work. |
| G-14 | Two accepted requests on the same local day retain separate command identities and only their own results. |
| G-15 | Retiring an old generation removes only its owned journal and cannot delete a live generation checkpoint. |
| G-16 | Revocation after an authorized read and before commit prevents the pending state transition from committing. |
| G-17 | A repeated acknowledgment after checkpoint compaction preserves the closed result and does not recreate state. |
| G-18 | Failed recovery for one stream leaves another readable with its exact accepted revision. |

### 4.2 Non-goals

1. This document does not authorize product implementation, installation, runtime permissions, deployment, or changes to compatibility policy.
2. It does not assert an existing protocol engine, state schema, external provider, UI, workflow, or test execution capability.
3. It does not replace, recount, or weaken the authentication baseline in `specs/foundation.md`.

### 4.3 Fixed product/safety invariants

1. Stale or unauthorized work must not overwrite separately accepted progress.
2. Recovery failure must preserve independently verified state; rollback must retain the original persisted version and remove all new transaction records.
3. Duplicate requests and acknowledgments must not recreate work or advance counters after acceptance/closure.
4. No scenario in this Draft constitutes a claim of executed verification.

## 5. Current versus proposed product journey

| Stage | Current | Proposed | User/operator effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qualification | Source fixture and three authentication baseline cases are documented | Maintainer reviews 18 separate protocol assertions | Scope and evidence expectations are inspectable |
| Evidence | No supplied evidence establishes these protocol behaviors | Future work may provide per-case evidence | Acceptance remains a maintainer decision |
| Publication | `docs:check` is the only declared project script | Any future publication must preserve companion and owner relationship | No absent SDK validation command is prescribed |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Issue #47 request] --> B[Draft companion with 18 planned cases]
    B --> C[Future reviewed evidence, if implemented]
    C --> D[Maintainer accepts or records gap]
```

Text equivalent: issue request -> Draft defines assertions -> future evidence is reviewed -> maintainer records acceptance or an open gap.

## 6. Functional behavior and state model

### 6.1 Happy path

1. The maintainer reviews the distinct case identities and assertions below without treating them as executed tests.
2. If future implementation work is separately authorized, its evidence can be assessed against each case while the three foundation baseline cases remain in force.
3. The maintainer records whether each observable assertion is satisfied; this Draft alone does not change status to Ready or implemented.

### 6.2 Alternative paths

- If evidence conflicts with an assertion, preserve the exact discrepancy for maintainer resolution rather than silently aliasing or dropping a case.
- If a requested outcome cannot be mapped to an observed product surface, that surface remains an explicit unknown.

### 6.3 State machine

Duplicate, stale, out-of-order, canceled, and partially completed protocol events have the explicit expected outcomes in cases G-03, G-07–G-10, G-13–G-18. Their storage and implementation mechanics remain unspecified.

## 7. User-facing configuration

No user-facing configuration is introduced by this authored qualification request. Stop instant, clock source, local-day interpretation, generation identity, and recovery source are scenario inputs for future acceptance, not proposed public settings. ## 16. Acceptance

These are planned, executable acceptance scenarios for a future implementation and maintainer review; none is claimed executed.

1. Given a restored checkpoint without bootstrap state, when no explicit bootstrap occurs, then no initial work is created; when bootstrap is explicitly requested, exactly one generation is recorded (G-01).
2. Given a full final scan chunk whose lookahead contains only seen records, when the scan closes, then it closes at the exact unique-record boundary without an empty extra cycle (G-02).
3. Given a current generation and a completion token from the previous generation, when the token is replayed, then the current generation is neither completed nor reopened (G-03).
4. Given two independent journals at the same high revision, when one is resumed, then the other journal’s checkpoint is not consumed (G-04).
5. Given persisted storage version nine and a late migration failure, when migration rolls back, then every new record is absent and version nine remains (G-05).
6. Given an item exactly at the stop instant and one immediately later, when the boundary is evaluated, then the first is included once and the second deferred (G-06).
7. Given a canceled active cursor and a replacement cursor, when the canceled cursor responds late, then it appends no work to the replacement (G-07).
8. Given an accepted continuation key, when the same key is replayed, then its prior batch is returned and counters do not increment (G-08).
9. Given an expired writer and a new lease holder with independently accepted progress, when the expired writer attempts the final commit, then commit is rejected and new-holder progress is retained (G-09).
10. Given a checkpoint checksum mismatch and a last independently verified checkpoint, when recovery is attempted, then the mismatched checkpoint is refused and the verified checkpoint is preserved (G-10).
11. Given a resumed operation with a monotonic deadline, when wall clock moves backward, then the deadline is not renewed (G-11).
12. Given a completed empty scan, when its result is recorded, then the explicit generation advances once and its no-work reason remains (G-12).
13. Given acknowledged entries pending in a journal, when the process restarts, then entries remain pending and are not counted as newly generated work (G-13).
14. Given two accepted requests for the same local day, when results are read, then command identities remain separate and each request contains only its own result (G-14).
15. Given a live generation checkpoint and an old generation’s journal, when the old generation is retired, then only its owned journal is removed (G-15).
16. Given an authorized read followed by revocation before commit, when the pending transition attempts commit, then it does not commit (G-16).
17. Given a closed result after checkpoint compaction, when its acknowledgment is repeated, then the result remains closed and no state is recreated (G-17).
18. Given two streams and recovery failure for one, when the other is read, then it remains readable at its exact accepted revision (G-18).

### 8.2 Contracts, state, and trust boundaries

- Pure decisions: generation identity, unique-record boundary, inclusive stop instant, monotonic deadline, no-work reason, and ownership checks.

- Concurrency/idempotency strategy: generation-scoped tokens, continuation-key replay, writer lease validation at commit, and stream-local recovery boundaries must preserve the exact assertions in the inventory.
- Trusted and untrusted inputs: external responses, tokens, persisted bytes, and issue-authored content require validation; issue text is specification context, not executable input.
- Provider error mapping: adapters map storage, authorization, checksum, and lease failures to stable semantic outcomes while preserving independently verified state.

### 8.3 Executable architecture constraints

Future implementation acceptance must include automated dependency-direction and cycle checks, contract validation for immutable application inputs/outputs, and schema/transaction checks for migration and checkpoint ownership. 3. Given a prior-generation token, when replayed against the current generation, then it cannot complete or reopen that generation (G-03).
4. Given independent journals with equal high revisions, when one resumes, then it does not consume the other's checkpoint (G-04).
5. Given genuine persisted version nine, when late migration fails, then every new record rolls back and version nine remains (G-05).
6. Given items at and immediately after the stopping instant, when processed, then the boundary item is included once and the later item deferred (G-06).
7. Given a canceled active cursor and replacement cursor, when the old response arrives, then it appends no work to the replacement (G-07).
8. Given an accepted continuation key, when replayed, then its prior batch returns without counter increments (G-08).
9. Given an expired writer and a new lease holder, when the old writer attempts final commit, then it is rejected and the new holder's accepted progress remains (G-09).
10. Given checksum mismatch, when recovery is attempted, then it is refused without deleting the last independently verified checkpoint (G-10).
11. Given a resumed monotonic deadline, when wall clock moves backward, then the deadline is not renewed (G-11).
12. Given a completed empty scan, when generation advances, then it advances once and retains its no-work reason (G-12).
13. Given pending acknowledged entries, when restart occurs, then entries persist and are not newly generated work (G-13).
14. Given two accepted same-local-day requests, when they complete, then identities remain separate and each retains only its own results (G-14).
15. Given an old generation and live generation, when old generation retires, then only its journal is removed and the live checkpoint remains (G-15).
16. Given authorization revoked after read and before commit, when commit is attempted, then the transition is prevented (G-16).
17. Given a closed result and compacted checkpoint, when acknowledgment repeats, then result remains closed and no state is recreated (G-17).
18. Given recovery failure for one stream, when another stream is read, then the other remains readable at its exact accepted revision (G-18).

# Grounded Project Verification and Acceptance

- Status: Draft
- Date: 2026-11-04
- Catalog capability ID: fixture-foundation
- Last verified: not applicable (prospective companion; source reviewed at the selected revision)
- Owners: Fixture maintainer; maintainer owns acceptance
- Scope: Define bounded repository-documentation and SDK-specification-consistency acceptance guidance for the existing fixture-foundation capability.

> Start with the repository standard in [`README.md`](./README.md). Remove this note when the spec is ready. Mark a non-applicable section explicitly and give a reason instead of silently deleting the concern.

## 1. Executive summary

This companion qualifies how maintainers verify repository documentation and assess consistency with the SDK specification standard for the actual selected project. The recommended default is to inspect and validate documentation and specification facts against the immutable repository tree, while distinguishing declared commands from checks actually run. The governing correctness rule is that evidence must be source-grounded: a command name or standard example does not prove that the selected project implements that check.

```text
Maintainer reviews the companion -> checks cited repository facts and documented guidance -> records documentation and specification-consistency evidence -> decides acceptance
```

This is an authored qualification request, not consumer implementation. The existing foundation contract and its three baseline cases remain required and unchanged. No runtime permissions, installation, source implementation, or compatibility policy changes are in scope.

## 2. Problem, current behavior, and evidence

### 2.1 Problem

Maintainers need usable verification guidance for this selected source and a clear acceptance standard for documentation and SDK-specification consistency. A generic command copied from a standard can mislead when the selected project does not declare it or its scope is narrower than the standard’s validation goals. Acceptance must not mistake documentation checks, declared scripts, or proposed scenarios for executed SDK validation.

### 2.2 Current behavior

Verified source facts:

1. `package.json` declares `pnpm@10.12.4` and only the `docs:check` script, invoking `node scripts/check-docs.cjs`.
2. `scripts/check-docs.cjs` checks that `docs/payments.mdx` exists; it does not establish SDK specification or catalog validation.
3. `docs/commands.md` documents `pnpm run docs:check` and explicitly says no successful run is claimed.
4. The selected catalog lists `fixture-foundation` as implemented with `specs/foundation.md`, `app/core.py`, `checks/test_core.py`, and `docs/payments.mdx`; its workflows array is empty.
5. `specs/foundation.md` owns three retained baseline cases: `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03`.

Proposed behavior: acceptance checks documentation against actual repository content, and separately reviews specification consistency against the standard and catalog evidence. The concrete invocation for SDK specification/catalog validation remains unverified; this companion does not prescribe an absent script or installation step.

### 2.3 Evidence

- Code/workflow/documentation references: `package.json`; `scripts/check-docs.cjs`; `docs/commands.md`; `specs/README.md`; `specs/catalog.json`; `specs/foundation.md`; `docs/source-evidence.md`; `docs/payments.mdx`; `app/core.py`; `checks/test_core.py`. No workflow files are present in the selected file inventory.
- Source identity: `docs/source-evidence.md` records `specs/foundation.md` Git blob `16f39aed096aae5cd8dee237d607ae606e802d2e` and SHA-256 `7edf1cb9ad46f8c06db97ecef6c8ddb4bc06bcb2a7793a1f4c6c8533a205ad60`. These identify the authored file bytes and do not establish runtime execution.
- Incidents or concrete examples: no incident evidence supplied. The declared documentation check only checks presence of `docs/payments.mdx`; treating it as full specification/catalog validation would overstate its evidenced scope.
- External primary sources: none required for this repository-specific qualification.
- Unknowns: whether a separate SDK validator is installed or available in the maintainer environment; no execution or successful validation is evidenced. No runtime behavior is inferred beyond inspected source.

### 2.4 Retrospective classification (as-built baselines only)

Not applicable: this is a prospective companion and reconstructs no implemented baseline. The owning `specs/foundation.md` remains the existing contract; its three baseline cases are references, not new cases in this companion.

## 3. Actors, surfaces, and terminology

| Actor | Goal | Entry point | Visible surfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixture maintainer | Review grounded guidance and decide acceptance | Issue #47 and proposed companion | GitHub issue, specification, repository documentation, review evidence |
| Documentation contributor | Keep documentation claims and navigation accurate | Documentation change | `docs/payments.mdx`, `docs/commands.md`, review |
| Specification reviewer | Assess conformance without overstating evidence | Companion and catalog | `specs/grounding-guidance.md`, `specs/foundation.md`, `specs/catalog.json` |

“Documentation check” means the observed `docs:check` behavior only. “Specification consistency” means a maintainer assessment that specification metadata, ownership, cited paths, requirements, cases, and documentation references agree with the selected source and applicable standard. It is not synonymous with `docs:check`. “Acceptance evidence” is a recorded review result; a drafted scenario is not an executed test. The maintainer owns acceptance facts and decisions.

## 4. Goals

| Requirement | Behavior |
|---|---|
| G-01 | Provide documentation guidance grounded in existing files and accurately scoped repository commands. |
| G-02 | Require maintainer review of SDK-specification consistency against inspected source and catalog evidence, without claiming execution. |
| G-03 | Preserve foundation ownership and its three retained baseline cases while keeping this companion bounded to qualification guidance. |
| G-04 | Keep acceptance, permissions, installation, implementation, and compatibility scope limited to the authored request. |

### 4.1 Goals

1. G-01: A maintainer can verify documented command claims against the package declaration and exact script behavior.
2. G-02: A maintainer can record whether specification claims, paths, catalog ownership, and documentation references are consistent with selected source evidence.
3. G-03: The companion supplements `specs/foundation.md`; it does not redefine that owner or duplicate its baseline cases.
4. G-04: Acceptance is a maintainer decision based on reviewable evidence, not an implementation activity or presumed passing command.

### 4.2 Non-goals

1. Add or change runtime behavior, source implementation, authentication behavior, or tests for the foundation.
2. Install SDK tooling, add scripts or workflows, grant runtime permissions, or alter compatibility policy.
3. Claim that the SDK validator ran or that `docs:check` performs specification/catalog validation.

### 4.3 Fixed product/safety invariants

1. Evidence claims MUST match inspected source and exact invocation scope.
2. Proposed acceptance cases MUST never be represented as executed tests.
3. Existing foundation ownership and all three baseline cases MUST remain intact.
4. Maintainer acceptance owns the qualification decision; no runtime authorization is introduced.

## 5. Current versus proposed product journey

| Discover checks | `docs/commands.md` names `pnpm run docs:check`; no successful run is claimed | Guidance states the declared invocation and inspected behavior precisely | Maintainer knows what the command establishes |

| Decide | No companion qualification outcome is evidenced | Maintainer records review evidence and disposition | Clear, inspectable acceptance responsibility |

The flow is: maintainer consults repository guidance -> checks source and documented command scope -> reviews specification/catalog consistency -> records acceptance decision. These are review transitions, not automated runtime states.

## 6. Functional behavior and state model

### 6.1 Happy path

1. The contributor updates the companion and cites exact repository-relative evidence.
2. The maintainer checks command declarations and the referenced script definition, then checks specification and catalog statements against source.
3. The maintainer records acceptance only after both documentation and specification-consistency review are satisfactory; otherwise the draft remains Draft with the unresolved issue identified.

### 6.2 Alternative paths

- If a cited path or command is absent, record the gap and state the required validation outcome without inventing an invocation.
- If documentation presence passes but specification consistency is not established, acceptance remains incomplete.
- If acceptance is deferred, retain the Draft status and open decision; do not imply failure of the existing runtime capability.

### 6.3 State machine

| State | Entered when | User-visible meaning | Allowed next states | Recovery/owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Companion is proposed | Qualification is not ready for implementation | Review, blocked | Maintainer resolves evidence gap |
| Review | Maintainer assesses documented evidence | Acceptance is under human review | Accepted, blocked, Draft | Maintainer records findings |
| Blocked | Required invocation or evidence remains unresolved | No readiness claim can be made | Review, Draft | Maintainer verifies prerequisite or narrows claim |
| Accepted | Documentation and consistency review evidence is recorded | Qualification request is accepted | Draft on material change | Maintainer owns disposition |

No duplicate, stale, asynchronous, canceled, or partially completed runtime events apply; this is a documentation and review contract. Re-review after material source changes is a maintainer responsibility.

## 7. User-facing configuration

Not applicable: the companion introduces no product or runtime configuration. The only invocation discussed is the existing declared command `pnpm run docs:check`; it is documentation of an existing project command, not a new configurable input. ## 8. Clean Architecture

| Application | Maintainer review checklist and acceptance disposition | Runtime orchestration or consumer implementation |

This is a specification-only change, so no application layers or runtime dependencies are added. Textual flow: repository files and declarations -> maintainer evidence review -> acceptance disposition shown in the companion/review.

### 8.2 Contracts, state, and trust boundaries

- Pure decisions: classify a statement as verified only when cited selected source supports it; distinguish declaration, inspection, invocation, and successful execution.
- Application contracts: maintainer records evidence reviewed and a disposition; no machine-readable runtime API is introduced.

### 8.3 Executable architecture constraints

No application dependency boundary is changed, so architecture dependency tests are not applicable. Review constraint: do not introduce implementation claims or runtime modules in this companion. Repository document structure and case/traceability consistency are checked by the publication process; this is a publication consistency check, not runtime or security acceptance. The selected project provides no evidenced SDK specification/catalog validation invocation, so an executable constraint for that validator remains unresolved and blocks readiness.

## 9. UI/UX and content contract

The primary surface is the GitHub issue and specification review. Status must say whether evidence review is pending, blocked, or accepted; identify completed evidence; name the next maintainer action; and link to inspectable repository files. No runtime action is required.

### 9.1 Information hierarchy

## 14. Testing strategy

This qualification inventory defines executable review/publication acceptance scenarios, not executed tests. The foundation cases `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03` remain required under their owner and are not counted in this companion’s budget. The new cases below cover documentation command scope, source consistency, and accurate acceptance reporting.

{{SDD_CASE_BUDGET}}

### 4.1 Goals

1. Meet the grounding and qualification behaviors in G-01 through G-04.

### 4.2 Non-goals

2. Defining a compatibility policy or claiming that source inspection proves execution.
3. Replacing or duplicating the foundation owner’s baseline contract.

### 4.3 Fixed product/safety invariants

1. A source citation supports only the facts visible in that source; declaration is not execution.
2. An unknown invocation or prerequisite stays visible until supported by selected-source evidence and maintainer decision.

## 5. Current versus proposed product journey

| Acceptance | Maintainer ownership is specified by the issue | Maintainer evaluates scenarios and blockers | Clear decision and next action |

Three transitions: selected source -> evidence classification -> maintainer acceptance. Text equivalent: inspect selected files -> record facts and unknowns -> maintainer accepts or returns the Draft with blockers.

## 6. Functional behavior and state model

### 6.1 Happy path

1. Author identifies the exact selected revision and cites actual repository-relative files.
2. Author labels each material statement as verified, proposed, or unknown.
3. Author records validation outcomes without naming an unsupported executable invocation.
4. Maintainer checks scenarios, traceability, retained baseline references, and readiness blockers, then records acceptance or requested clarification.

### 6.2 Alternative paths

- If a cited file does not support a claim, narrow or remove the claim and retain uncertainty.
- If validation prerequisites remain unknown, the SDD stays Draft and the invocation is not run or invented.
- If acceptance finds a gap, the maintainer returns a specific evidence or behavior question; no runtime action follows from this specification.

### 6.3 State machine

| State | Entered when | User-visible meaning | Allowed next states | Recovery/owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft grounded | Source facts and uncertainty are cited | Proposed qualification is reviewable | Review pending | Author supplies evidence |
| Review pending | Maintainer begins acceptance review | No acceptance decision yet | Accepted; clarification needed | Maintainer owns review |
| Clarification needed | Claim, evidence, or decision is incomplete | Draft is not ready | Draft grounded | Author resolves or records blocker |
| Accepted | Maintainer confirms scenarios and blockers resolved | Authored qualification accepted | Later revision only by review | Maintainer records decision |

Duplicate reviews do not create additional acceptance facts; newest review must refer to the same selected revision or identify the changed revision. Out-of-order evidence is not silently applied to another revision. Cancellation leaves the Draft and its known facts intact. Partial review is not acceptance.

## 7. User-facing configuration

No runtime or user configuration is introduced. The only review input is the selected source revision, fixed for each qualification pass. A later revision requires a new evidence review. There are no configurable permissions, URLs, commands, secrets, or execution modes. Validation rejects unsupported factual claims; absent, retired, and future configuration migration is not applicable because no configuration schema is proposed.

Recommended review: read-only inspection of the selected immutable revision and authored files. Meaningful alternative: defer qualification until the unresolved toolchain/invocation question is answered. Neither option weakens the invariant that claims require evidence.

### 8.1 Responsibilities and dependency direction

|---|---|---|
| Domain/pure policy | Evidence classification, requirement-to-case completeness, readiness rules | Runtime, provider, or framework behavior |
| Application | Qualification review input/output and acceptance decision record | Concrete SDK/process invocation |
| Adapters/data | Reading selected source facts and presenting citations | Product acceptance policy |
| Infrastructure/composition | Any future approved source-selection integration | Business decisions; none is proposed here |
| Entrypoints | Issue/review event interpretation by a future authorized process | Duplicated acceptance logic or command execution implied by this SDD |
| Presentation | Review status, evidence links, and maintainer next action | Mutations or acceptance policy |


Text equivalent: maintainer review enters qualification policy, which consults cited source evidence and produces a review summary.

### 8.2 Contracts, state, and trust boundaries

### 8.3 Executable architecture constraints

A future implementation must automatically check citation existence and requirement/case reciprocity against the selected revision and reject unsupported repository paths. The concrete checker and invocation are unknown and remain a readiness blocker; no repository validation script is evidenced. Human review must confirm claim scope. These requirements are acceptance criteria, not evidence that checks exist or have passed.

Record the prerequisite or keep this Draft.” Partial: “Evidence review is complete, but product acceptance remains pending; cited facts are retained and no acceptance decision is implied.” Complete: “Maintainer accepted this authored qualification for the reviewed revision; this records no runtime execution or implementation.”

### 9.3 Issue, PR, and comment behavior

- Deterministic title: “Grounded project verification and acceptance”. Purpose: record qualification requirements for issue #47.
- Merge, close, or retry has no prescribed runtime effect; only a maintainer’s explicit review records acceptance.
- Durable marker/idempotent updates: issue URL and reviewed revision identify the decision; edits update the existing review context rather than creating repeated status comments.
- Comment/notification budget: at most one status comment per review decision; revisions update the existing summary where supported.
- Labels and checks are supplemental and cannot replace acceptance.
- Links use descriptive destinations to issue and owning SDD; unavailable destinations are omitted rather than fabricated.

### 9.4 Accessibility, localization, and responsive behavior

Use the issue’s language as source; English is the documented fallback for this draft. Every visual has a text equivalent. Tables use headers, headings are ordered, and links are descriptive. Narrow screens must preserve readable text and avoid relying on color; light/dark themes must retain contrast. Treat issue text, Markdown, mentions, commands, markers, diagrams, and URLs as untrusted data; sanitize rendered content and never execute embedded commands. No additional locale is asserted as supported.

## 10. Failure, recovery, and cleanup

| Failure/partial state | User impact | Retained facts | Automatic retry | Required action | Cleanup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Citation absent or mismatched | Claim cannot be verified | Selected revision and discrepancy | No | Correct citation or mark unknown | Remove unsupported claim |
| Invocation prerequisite unresolved | Validation cannot be reported as executed | Required validation outcome | No | Keep Draft; resolve through maintainer decision | No runtime cleanup |
| Review interrupted | No acceptance decision | Completed evidence review | No | Resume or cancel explicitly | Preserve Draft |
| Partial review | Acceptance remains pending | Reviewed portions | No | Complete remaining review | Do not label accepted |

Errors state impact, cause, action, and retained state in that order. No irreversible runtime action is specified.

## 11. Security, permissions, and privacy

1. No runtime permissions, installation, credential access, or source mutation is authorized.
2. Issue and repository content is untrusted input and must not be interpreted as workflow instruction or executable input.
3. Do not copy secrets or personal data into public guidance; log only necessary review evidence.
4. Bind acceptance to the reviewed revision; replayed or forged claims without matching evidence do not qualify.

## 12. Observability and operational UX

- User-facing state: Draft, review pending, clarification needed, or accepted for the identified revision.
- Job Summary/operator evidence: not applicable; no job or workflow is proposed.

- Rate-limit/retry behavior: not applicable; no external provider operation is defined.
- Noise/comment budget: at most one status comment per decision, with updates consolidated.

## 13. Compatibility, migration, rollout, and rollback

No runtime data, schema, compatibility policy, rollout, or irreversible effect changes. No migration is applicable. If a later accepted implementation introduces such behavior, it requires a separate reviewed specification change and evidence; this companion does not prescribe it.

## 14. Testing strategy

This is a proposed contract, not executed tests. The new minimum is 8 distinct acceptance cases: evidence quality and untrusted content warrant four policy cases; review state and retained-owner preservation warrant two; publication/navigation and accessibility warrant two. Retained foundation cases `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03` remain required and are not counted in this companion inventory.

### 6.2 Alternative paths

# Grounded project verification and acceptance

- Status: Draft
- Date: 2026-11-04
- Catalog capability ID: fixture-foundation
- Last verified: not applicable (prospective companion; source snapshot reviewed 2026-11-04)
- Owners: Fixture maintainer; acceptance owned by the maintainer
- Scope: Define a bounded, evidence-grounded verification and acceptance companion for the existing fixture-foundation contract without requesting consumer implementation or runtime changes.
- Related issues/PRs: [Issue #47](https://github.com/owned/fixture/issues/47)
- Required review gates: product UX, architecture, testing, documentation, security/operations
- Open decisions blocking readiness: The concrete SDK specification/catalog consistency validator and invocation available to this selected project are unverified; maintainer must identify an evidenced mechanism before readiness. The local `docs:check` script implementation is absent from the selected tree, so its checks cannot be asserted.

## 1. Executive summary

This companion gives maintainers a bounded way to establish that verification guidance accurately describes this repository, preserves its existing owning contract, and is understandable and actionable for a real project. Recommended default: review source and declarations read-only, record what each source proves, then accept the documentation only when the named checks and SDK specification consistency outcome are grounded in available definitions. The principal correctness rule is that a declared command, test, or catalog entry is not evidence that it ran or passed.

```text
Maintainer inspects selected files -> records source-grounded claims and limits -> checks docs and owning-spec consistency -> accepts or records a blocker
```

## 2. Problem, current behavior, and evidence

### 2.1 Problem

Maintainers and reviewers need guidance that is useful for this selected project rather than copied from a generic SDK example. Without checking the actual source, guidance can name unavailable scripts, overstate a command's coverage, or present planned cases as executed tests. This would weaken confidence in both repository documentation and the foundation capability's contract.

### 2.2 Current behavior

1. The catalog identifies `fixture-foundation` as implemented, owned by Fixture maintainer, and links its owning specification and evidence paths.
2. `specs/foundation.md` is Draft and contains two requirements, three explicit retained cases, and documentation path declarations.
3. The selected tree declares `pnpm@10.12.4` and one package script, `docs:check`, invoking `node scripts/check-docs.cjs`.
4. `scripts/check-docs.cjs` is not present in the selected file listing. Its behavior and successful execution are unverified. No `validate:specifications` script is declared in the selected `package.json`.
5. The source entrypoint `app/core.py` defines only `identity(value)`, and `checks/test_core.py` contains one identity assertion. These do not evidence execution of the foundation's retained authentication/publication cases.

### 2.3 Evidence

- Code/workflow/documentation references: `specs/catalog.json`; `specs/foundation.md`; `specs/README.md`; `specs/CATALOG.md`; `specs/_template.md`; `package.json`; `docs/commands.md`; `docs/source-evidence.md`; `app/core.py`; `checks/test_core.py`; `docs/payments.mdx`.
- The repository command guide names `pnpm run docs:check`, and package metadata declares that command, but the referenced script file is absent from the selected tree. No verification of its behavior or execution is claimed.
- `docs/source-evidence.md` records the owning specification Git blob `16f39aed096aae5cd8dee237d607ae606e802d2e` and SHA-256 `7edf1cb9ad46f8c06db97ecef6c8ddb4bc06bcb2a7793a1f4c6c8533a205ad60`. Those identities apply to the source snapshot, not to execution.
- Incidents or concrete examples: the selected package script points to an unobserved script path; the SDK standard describes `pnpm run validate:specifications`, but this selected package does not declare it. The documented SDK invocation therefore cannot be asserted as available here.
- External primary sources: none required for this repository-specific qualification.
- Unknowns: behavior of `docs:check`; the SDK consistency validator/tooling and its exact invocation for this selected consumer; CI execution and results; whether documentation examples are rendered or checked elsewhere.

### 2.4 Retrospective classification (as-built baselines only)

Not applicable: this is a prospective companion and does not reconstruct an implemented verification capability. The current facts above are source observations, not an as-built contract for new behavior.

## 3. Actors, surfaces, and terminology

| Actor | Goal | Entry point | Visible surfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixture maintainer | Accept useful, accurate verification guidance | Issue #47 and companion review | Issue, pull request/review, specification, project docs |
| Reviewer | Confirm claims are supported and limits explicit | Companion and cited source files | Specification, source tree, review comments |
| Contributor | Follow documented checks without guessing | Project command and specification docs | `docs/commands.md`, `specs/README.md`, owning and companion SDDs |

“Selected source” means files present in the immutable project snapshot under review. “Source-grounded claim” means a statement tied to inspected bytes or declarations. “Verification invocation” means an exact command whose execution context and declaration are evidenced. “SDK consistency acceptance” means an explicit review outcome that the companion agrees with the owning SDD and the repository's specification standard; it does not imply a validator ran. The maintainer owns acceptance facts. The companion supplements, and does not replace, `specs/foundation.md` or its three baseline cases: `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03`.

## 4. Goals

### 4.1 Goals

| Requirement | Behavior |
|---|---|
| G-01 | Verification guidance MUST cite actual selected files and distinguish inspected declarations from command execution or test results. |
| G-02 | Repository documentation checks MUST state only the evidenced invocation and scope; unavailable or uninspected implementations remain explicitly unverified. |
| G-03 | SDK specification consistency acceptance MUST compare this companion with the owning SDD and applicable repository standard, while leaving any unavailable validator invocation unresolved. |
| G-04 | Acceptance MUST preserve the owning specification and all three retained baseline cases; this companion adds no runtime implementation, permissions, installation, or compatibility policy. |
| G-05 | Documentation MUST provide a practical maintainer review path, evidence limitations, and an explicit blocked outcome when required verification cannot be established. |

### 4.2 Non-goals

1. Implementing product behavior, changing authentication/publication semantics, or claiming that baseline cases passed.
2. Installing SDK tools, adding scripts or workflows, changing permissions, or setting a compatibility policy.
3. Replacing, editing, or restating the owning foundation contract; the companion is additive.

### 4.3 Fixed product/safety invariants

1. Source declarations are not execution results. Acceptance MUST not claim a command ran or passed without recorded execution evidence.
2. The existing owning specification and its retained baseline cases remain required and authoritative for foundation behavior.
3. Maintainable guidance MUST not turn an absent or unverified invocation into an installation requirement or invented command.

## 5. Current versus proposed product journey

| Stage | Current | Proposed | User/operator effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Establish source | Catalog and docs identify files; no companion process is specified | Maintainer inspects actual declarations and files before making claims | Review begins from reproducible repository facts |
| Check documentation | `docs:check` is declared, but its target implementation is absent in the selected tree | Guidance records exact invocation and labels its implementation/scope unverified | Maintainer does not mistake a name for coverage |
| Check specification consistency | Standard describes SDK validation, while selected package has no such script declaration | Compare owning SDD, companion, standard, and catalog evidence; record any validator prerequisite as unresolved | Acceptance remains reviewable without fabricating a check |
| Accept | No companion acceptance criteria exist | Maintainer records pass or blocker against the scenarios below | Clear decision and next action |

## 6. Functional behavior and state model

### 6.1 Happy path

1. The maintainer locates the catalog owner and inspects the cited files in the selected tree.
2. The maintainer records exact command/tool declarations, execution context, and the definition each check references, if present.
3. The maintainer compares companion claims with the owning SDD and standard, preserving ownership and baseline cases.
4. The maintainer accepts only supported documentation and consistency outcomes, recording unavailable verification as a blocker rather than a pass.

### 6.2 Alternative paths

- If a command declaration exists but its entrypoint is absent, document the declaration and absent definition; do not describe its checks or require it as executable.
- If no SDK consistency validator invocation is evidenced, perform and record a human consistency review while retaining the concrete validator/invocation as a readiness blocker.
- If source evidence conflicts with prose, correct the prose to match the inspected source or mark the fact unresolved.

### 6.3 State machine

| State | Entered when | User-visible meaning | Allowed next states | Recovery/owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Companion proposed | Guidance awaits maintainer review | Evidence reviewed, Blocked | Fixture maintainer gathers source evidence |
| Evidence reviewed | Claims have citations and limitations | Documentation claims are grounded | Accepted, Blocked | Reviewer records findings |
| Blocked | Required invocation or evidence is unavailable | Acceptance is incomplete; no successful check is implied | Evidence reviewed | Maintainer supplies verified definition/result or documents an allowed manual outcome |
| Accepted | All applicable scenarios pass and blockers resolved or explicitly excluded from readiness as non-blocking | Companion is suitable for its authored purpose | Draft on material change | Maintainer owns acceptance record |

Duplicate reviews do not create duplicate requirements; newer evidence supersedes an earlier observation only when tied to a specific source snapshot. Out-of-order claims without source evidence remain unaccepted. Cancellation or partial review leaves the document Draft or Blocked.

## 7. User-facing configuration

Not applicable: this documentation qualification introduces no runtime or user configuration. Review scope is fixed to the selected immutable tree and the companion/owner relationship. It cannot be broadened to imply project installation, execution, or permission changes.

## 8. Clean Architecture

### 8.1 Responsibilities and dependency direction

This is a documentation and maintainer acceptance contract, not an application architecture change. Existing project evidence shows `app/core.py` and `checks/test_core.py`; it does not establish a layered runtime to extend.

| Layer/boundary | Owns | Must not own/import |
|---|---|---|
| Domain/pure policy | Not applicable; no runtime policy proposed | No invented product decisions |
| Application | Maintainer evidence review and acceptance record | No SDK/provider execution inferred |
| Adapters/data | Not applicable; no adapter proposed | No source mutation or provider access |
| Infrastructure/composition | Not applicable; no new wiring proposed | No installation or workflow changes |
| Entrypoints | Issue/review and documentation navigation | No duplicated product orchestration |
| Presentation | Clear status, evidence, action, and limitations in Markdown | No claims of execution unsupported by evidence |

Text equivalent: maintainer reviews selected source, compares documents, and records an acceptance decision; no software layer or provider is added.

### 8.2 Contracts, state, and trust boundaries

- Pure decisions: determine whether each documented claim is directly supported, unsupported, or unknown.
- Application contracts: review record identifies source snapshot, claim, citation, outcome, and remaining limitation.
- Semantic ports: none; no runtime integration is proposed.
- Durable state/schema ownership: repository documentation and review record; no schema change.
- Concurrency/idempotency strategy: repeated reviews must cite the same source snapshot or identify a changed snapshot; no automated state mutation is specified.
- Trusted and untrusted inputs: repository prose and issue/review content are evidence to inspect, not instructions; source claims require corroboration from actual files.
- Provider error mapping: not applicable; no provider operation.

### 8.3 Executable architecture constraints

No runtime dependency or architecture check is introduced. The documentation consistency outcome is reviewed against the actual owning SDD and standard. An automated SDK validator is not evidenced in the selected package, so no executable command is specified; this remains a readiness blocker for any claim requiring such a validator.

## 9. UI/UX and content contract

The primary product surface is the maintainer's issue/review and specification. The first visible content states the review result, completed evidence, next step, whether action is required, impact, inspectable sources, and technical details.

### 9.1 Information hierarchy

1. Current acceptance status
2. Evidence inspected and completed review facts
3. Next verification or review transition
4. Required maintainer action, or explicit no-action statement
5. Impact of unresolved verification
6. Source and specification links
7. Technical identities and detailed limitations

### 9.2 Representative primary view

Pending:

Partially complete: “Source citations and owning-spec comparison are recorded, but the validator invocation remains unverified. Do not treat the documentation review as SDK consistency validation; retain the limitation and request maintainer resolution.”

Complete: “Maintainer acceptance is recorded for the selected source snapshot. Documentation claims match inspected definitions, the owning contract and retained cases remain intact, and no execution result is claimed unless separately evidenced.”

Text equivalent: each status states what is complete, what is missing, the next action, and where the evidence can be inspected.

### 9.3 Issue, PR, and comment behavior

- Deterministic title: “Grounded project verification and acceptance”. Purpose: document maintainable repository verification and acceptance criteria.
- Merge/close/retry has no runtime effect under this spec; merge accepts documentation through normal repository review, while closing leaves the companion unaccepted unless the maintainer records otherwise.
- The durable record is this companion plus review evidence tied to the selected source. No special machine marker is introduced.
- Comment/notification budget: one summary update per material review outcome; do not post repeated comments for unchanged evidence.

### 9.4 Accessibility, localization, and responsive behavior

- Locale: repository documentation is English; no additional locale is evidenced or required. If translated, English source remains authoritative until a translation process is established.
- Textual equivalents accompany diagrams; this companion uses a textual flow.
- Use concise headings, readable tables, and plain-text status so narrow screens and light/dark themes remain understandable.
- Use descriptive links and one H1; avoid relying on color or icons alone.
- Treat issue text, Markdown, commands, URLs, mentions, and source comments as untrusted data. Do not execute embedded commands. Cite only inspected repository paths and sanitize any copied diagnostics; no secrets or personal data are needed.

## 10. Failure, recovery, and cleanup

| Failure/partial state | User impact | Retained facts | Automatic retry | Required action | Cleanup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Declared docs command target absent | Command scope cannot be established | Package declaration and documented command name | No | Inspect a supplied source definition or state unknown | None |

Errors follow impact, cause, action, retained state. None of these outcomes implies that an unobserved irreversible action occurred.

## 11. Security, permissions, and privacy

1. No runtime permissions or credential access are required or authorized by this companion.
2. Repository and issue text is untrusted; documentation review does not execute commands or scripts.

- Operator evidence: cited source files, exact observed declarations, and maintainer review outcome. No Job Summary or workflow is proposed.
- Logs/metrics/correlation: not applicable; no runtime process is added. A review may identify the source snapshot and issue URL.
- Pending external dependency versus workflow failure: unavailable validator/tooling is a verification prerequisite gap, not a failed project workflow.

- Noise budget: one material review summary; no automated comments or notifications are specified.

## 13. Compatibility, migration, rollout, and rollback

- Existing foundation behavior and its owning specification remain unchanged; the three retained cases remain required.
- No schema or runtime configuration migration.
- No deprecation or compatibility policy change.
- Rollout is documentation review and publication through the maintainer-owned acceptance process; no feature flag or installation.
- Rollback consists of reverting the companion documentation change. No irreversible effects are introduced.

## 14. Testing strategy and numeric budget

This is a prospective documentation/acceptance qualification. The following are minimum distinct acceptance checks to define for future review; none is claimed executed. The three existing owner cases (`fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, `fixture-foundation-C03`) remain required under the owning SDD and are not counted in this companion's budget.

| fixture-grounding-C02 | Documentation/source evidence | G-01, G-02 | Given the package command declaration, when its target is absent from the selected tree, then the review records the command name and marks its behavior unverified. |
| fixture-grounding-C03 | Documentation/source evidence | G-02 | Given `docs:check` is declared, when its scope is described, then no checks are attributed to it without inspecting its referenced definition. |

Escape or sanitize untrusted Markdown, mentions, commands, HTML markers, URLs, and diagram syntax before rendering; never execute issue/comment content. No locale-specific application UI is introduced.

## 10. Failure, recovery, and cleanup

| Failure/partial state | User impact | Retained facts | Automatic retry | Required action | Cleanup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source path or identity cannot be confirmed | Claim cannot be qualified | Claim and attempted citation | No | Maintainer requests exact evidence | Remove no source data; correct citation |
| Declared command entrypoint unavailable in selected tree | Command scope cannot be asserted | Package declaration and command note | No | Record unresolved scope; inspect only an authorized selected source | No generated artifacts |
| Documentation review succeeds but SDK consistency is unverified | Overall acceptance incomplete | Documentation result and revision | No | Resolve validator evidence or keep blocked | Preserve partial review record |
| Evidence contradicts claim | Acceptance rejected | Contradiction and source references | No | Contributor corrects or withdraws claim | Update review record without erasing audit context |
| Review system temporarily unavailable | Maintainer cannot record outcome | Prepared evidence locally in review context | Bounded manual retry | Retry when available; do not report acceptance | No external side effect until recorded |

Errors follow impact -> cause -> action -> retained state. No irreversible product effect is defined by this companion.

## 11. Security, permissions, and privacy

1. Acceptance is maintainer-owned and requires only ordinary read/review access; this proposal grants no runtime permissions or installation.
2. Treat repository content, issue text, comments, and contributor claims as untrusted; do not execute embedded commands or scripts as part of evidence review.
3. Do not copy credential values, secret-bearing script bodies, or unnecessary personal data into public documentation, summaries, or logs.
4. Bind evidence to the reviewed immutable source revision and issue/review identity; duplicate or forged claims do not constitute acceptance.

## 12. Observability and operational UX

- User-facing state: pending, action required, blocked, partial, accepted, or rejected, with the reviewed revision.
- Operator evidence: exact source paths, observed command declaration and entrypoint status, consistency outcome, reviewer, and unresolved items.
- Logs/metrics/correlation: no new telemetry requirement; review record and issue number provide correlation. Do not log secrets.
- Pending external dependency versus workflow failure: unavailable validation evidence is a qualification blocker, not evidence that a product workflow failed.
- Rate-limit/retry behavior: no automation specified; any manual re-review is bounded to a material evidence or source revision change.
- Noise budget: one summary update per material outcome transition.

## 13. Compatibility, migration, rollout, and rollback

No runtime data, schema, configuration, or in-flight operation changes are proposed. No compatibility policy changes or rollout are applicable. If the companion is later revised, preserve the owning specification and existing baseline case identities; update this companion and its review evidence together. Rollback consists of withdrawing this proposed qualification without altering implementation or owner contract.

## 14. Testing strategy

This is an authored qualification request, not consumer implementation. The following are minimum distinct proposed acceptance cases, not executed tests. The existing owner retains `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03`; those baseline cases are not counted in this companion budget. No repository-wide coverage threshold is evidenced in the selected tree. For any later implementation, preserve an established repository threshold if one is found; require 100% branch coverage of new pure evidence-classification policy and full changed-policy coverage, with deterministic fixtures and no live service or real waits. Parse structural contracts and ownership; do not rely on grep alone. Golden rendered examples must also have semantic assertions. Maintainer manually reviews readability, truthful scope, and narrow-screen rendering. These requirements do not claim any check has run.

## 15. Documentation and discoverability

Lead with the normal evidence-review path, then disclose command limitations, blockers, and architecture. The selected standard requires user, setup, operator, contributor, migration, and troubleshooting content as applicable; for this bounded maintainer qualification, setup/permissions, operator recovery, migration, and runtime configuration are explicitly not applicable because no setup, runtime, or data change is proposed. 2. Given the declared `docs:check` command and absent inspected entrypoint, when documentation evidence is assessed, then neither successful execution nor SDK consistency scope is claimed.
3. Given the standard and catalog, when SDK consistency is assessed, then required structure and ownership/evidence relationships receive explicit outcomes; absent concrete invocation evidence remains a readiness blocker.

7. Given hostile or malformed issue/comment text, when shown in the review summary, then it is rendered inert and cannot execute commands or forge acceptance.
8. Given acceptance is recorded, when the completed summary is viewed, then reviewer outcome, source revision, next action (or none), limitations, and inspectable links are clear and accessible.
9. Given the documentation inventory, when repository navigation is validated, then existing citations resolve and the companion is the only proposed new artifact; check declarations are not misrepresented as executed validation.

# Grounded project verification and acceptance

- Status: Draft
- Date: 2026-11-04
- Catalog capability ID: fixture-foundation
- Last verified: not applicable (prospective companion)
- Owners: Fixture maintainer; maintainer owns acceptance
- Scope: Specify bounded project verification and product acceptance refinements for the existing fixture-foundation capability without changing its implementation or policy.
- Related issues/PRs: [Issue #47](https://github.com/owned/fixture/issues/47)
- Required review gates: product UX, architecture, testing, documentation, security/operations
- Open decisions blocking readiness: None identified for this authored qualification request; readiness remains Draft pending maintainer review and evidence.

## 1. Executive summary

This companion clarifies how a maintainer grounds review in the selected project’s evidence, uses its existing documentation-check command accurately, and accepts the product contract. It is an authored qualification request, not a consumer implementation. The existing foundation SDD and its three baseline cases remain authoritative and required. The recommended default is to inspect the immutable project sources and run the declared project documentation check from the project root when verification is requested. A documentation check does not establish specification/catalog consistency or execute acceptance scenarios.

```text
Maintainer reviews source and contract -> invokes the evidenced documentation check -> evaluates product acceptance and catalog/format outcomes -> records review evidence
```

## 2. Problem, current behavior, and evidence

### 2.1 Problem

Maintainers need a bounded way to distinguish project documentation verification from specification/catalog validation and from product acceptance. Conflating these outcomes can overstate what was checked or imply tests ran when they did not.

### 2.2 Current behavior

1. The catalog identifies `fixture-foundation` as implemented and assigns `specs/foundation.md` as its existing SDD; its implementation evidence includes `app/core.py` and `checks/test_core.py`.
2. The selected project declares `npm@11.0.0` and the script `docs:check` in `package.json`.
3. `docs/commands.md` documents `npm run docs:check`. Its referenced script, `scripts/check-docs.cjs`, only checks that `docs/payments.mdx` exists. No command execution or pass result is claimed by this specification.
4. The foundation SDD defines retained baseline cases `fixture-foundation-C01`, `fixture-foundation-C02`, and `fixture-foundation-C03`. They remain required and are not redefined or counted in this companion’s new-case budget.
5. The repository standard describes specification/catalog validation outcomes, but this selected project does not declare `validate:specifications` or `generate:specifications` scripts. The concrete invocation for those outcomes is unverified; the docs check is not a substitute.

### 2.3 Evidence

- Code/workflow/documentation references: `package.json`; `scripts/check-docs.cjs`; `docs/commands.md`; `specs/README.md`; `specs/catalog.json`; `specs/CATALOG.md`; `specs/foundation.md`; `app/core.py`; `checks/test_core.py`; `docs/payments.mdx`.
- Incidents or concrete examples: No incident evidence supplied. Concrete risk: claiming a successful documentation command or catalog validation without execution/evidence.
- External primary sources: [Canonical issue #47](https://github.com/owned/fixture/issues/47).
- Unknowns: An executable invocation for full specification-format/catalog consistency checks is not established by the selected project declarations. Maintainer acceptance evidence and execution results remain to be supplied during review.

### 2.4 Retrospective classification (as-built baselines only)

Not applicable: this prospective companion does not reconstruct an implemented baseline. Existing baseline ownership and cases remain in `specs/foundation.md`.

## 3. Actors, surfaces, and terminology

| Actor | Goal | Entry point | Visible surfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixture maintainer | Qualify documentation, specification consistency, and product acceptance accurately | Issue #47 and project review | Issue, SDDs, project command output, documentation, catalog |

“Documentation verification” means the narrow check implemented by the declared `docs:check` script. “Specification/catalog consistency” means the required format, ownership, and catalog outcomes; the installed invocation is unverified. “Acceptance” means maintainer evaluation of observable scenarios, not a claim that they have been executed. The catalog and cited source files own repository facts; the maintainer owns acceptance decisions.

## 4. Goals

| Requirement | Behavior |
|---|---|
| G-01 | Identify and accurately qualify the selected project’s documented documentation-check command and its evidenced scope. |
| G-02 | Preserve the foundation SDD ownership and all three retained baseline case obligations. |
| G-03 | Require specification-format and catalog-consistency outcomes while keeping any unverified invocation explicit. |
| G-04 | Make maintainer-owned product acceptance observable and distinguish proposed scenarios from executed tests. |

### 4.1 Goals

1. A reviewer can identify the declared command, package manager, execution context, and exact narrow check without inferring broader validation.
2. The companion supplements rather than replaces the existing owner and its baseline cases.
3. Acceptance includes format/catalog consistency outcomes and concrete product scenarios, with no fabricated execution evidence.

### 4.2 Non-goals

1. No runtime permissions, installation, source implementation, compatibility policy, workflow, or consumer behavior changes.
2. No claim that the documentation check validates SDD format, catalog ownership, or acceptance behavior.
3. No change to the existing foundation contract or its retained cases.

### 4.3 Fixed product/safety invariants

1. A declared command is not a passing result; acceptance evidence must record what was actually reviewed or run.
2. A Draft remains a Draft until its readiness blockers and review gates are resolved.
3. Existing case identities remain owned by the foundation SDD; this companion defines only its new cases.

## 5. Current versus proposed product journey

| Stage | Current | Proposed | User/operator effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grounding | Project declares `npm@11.0.0`, `docs:check`, and documents `npm run docs:check` | Review the exact script scope before describing its result | Documentation check is not overstated |
| Contract review | Foundation owns three baseline cases | Keep all three required and add bounded companion scenarios | Ownership and case lineage remain clear |
| Consistency | Standard states format/catalog goals; installed validation invocation is unverified | Record consistency as an acceptance outcome and disclose unresolved execution prerequisite | No invented command or result |
| Acceptance | Maintainer owns acceptance | Evaluate scenario evidence and clearly distinguish planned from completed | Review status is actionable and truthful |

## 6. Functional behavior and state model

### 6.1 Happy path

1. The maintainer inspects repository evidence and the foundation SDD.
2. If checking documentation, the maintainer uses the documented project command from the project root: `npm run docs:check`. Its evidenced check is existence of `docs/payments.mdx` only.
3. The maintainer reviews format and catalog consistency as separate outcomes, recording any unavailable invocation as unverified.
4. The maintainer evaluates the acceptance scenarios and records evidence; this Draft does not assert they have run.

### 6.2 Alternative paths

- If the documentation command is not run, report it as not run; source inspection alone is not command execution.
- If a consistency invocation cannot be established, report the outcome as pending/unverified and identify the prerequisite without inventing a script or installation step.
- If the source or catalog differs from cited evidence in a later revision, re-ground the review against that revision before acceptance.

### 6.3 State machine

| State | Entered when | User-visible meaning | Allowed next states | Recovery/owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Companion is proposed | Requirements and cases are authored, not accepted | In review, blocked | Maintainer reviews evidence |
| In review | Maintainer evaluates contract | Evidence and outcomes are being assessed | Accepted, blocked | Maintainer records findings |
| Blocked | Required evidence or decision is unavailable | Acceptance cannot be concluded | In review | Maintainer supplies evidence or resolves prerequisite |
| Accepted | All required outcomes have review evidence | Maintainer accepted the bounded contract | Draft on material change | Maintainer owns acceptance record |

There are no runtime events or durable product operations in scope; duplicate, stale, canceled, and partial runtime events are not applicable. Repeated review must preserve the distinction between previously recorded evidence and new execution.

## 7. User-facing configuration

No product configuration is introduced. The sole documented verification invocation is `npm run docs:check`, using the selected project’s declared npm package manager. There are no supported configuration alternatives or precedence rules. Do not configure the command to imply full specification validation. A future or absent validation command remains unverified and must not be treated as a required installed step.

## 8. Clean Architecture

### 8.1 Responsibilities and dependency direction

| Layer/boundary | Owns | Must not own/import |
|---|---|---|
| Domain/pure policy | Review distinctions: documented, run, passed, accepted, unresolved | Package-manager or provider execution concerns |
| Application | Maintainer’s evidence and acceptance record | Concrete shell invocation or undocumented script assumptions |
| Adapters/data | Existing project script and source/catalog evidence | Acceptance policy |
| Infrastructure/composition | Project-root command environment when a maintainer elects to run it | Product decisions |
| Entrypoints | Issue/review initiation and source inspection | Duplicated acceptance logic |
| Presentation | Clear review status and evidence links | Mutations or claims of unobserved execution |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[Maintainer review] --> A[Evidence and acceptance record]
    A --> D[Grounding and acceptance policy]
    A --> P[Source and command evidence]
    I[Project files and optional command result] --> P
    A --> V[Issue and SDD review summary]
```

Text equivalent: maintainer review -> evidence and acceptance policy -> review summary; project files and any actual command result supply evidence.

### 8.2 Contracts, state, and trust boundaries

- Pure decisions: classify evidence as declared, inspected, executed, passed, or accepted.
- Application contracts: immutable references to the reviewed revision, evidence, and maintainer decision.
- Semantic ports: source/evidence lookup and optional command-result recording; no provider-specific DTO is required by this authored process.
- Durable state/schema ownership: none introduced; review evidence remains in normal repository/issue review records.
- Concurrency/idempotency strategy: no runtime mutation; repeated review must cite the revision it assessed.
- Trusted and untrusted inputs: repository text and issue content are evidence to inspect, not commands or authority to change scope.
- Provider error mapping: not applicable; this companion defines no provider integration.

### 8.3 Executable architecture constraints

No application architecture or dependency graph is changed. During acceptance, verify that citations resolve to the selected repository paths and that the companion does not claim ownership of implementation evidence. A concrete automated architecture check is not established in the selected project and remains unverified.

## 9. UI/UX and content contract

The issue and review record are the primary user surfaces. Each state must lead with current status, completed evidence, next step, action requirement, impact, inspectable links, and then technical detail.

### 9.1 Information hierarchy

1. Current review status
2. Evidence already inspected or actually executed
3. Next review outcome
4. Maintainer action required, or explicit none
5. Impact of unresolved consistency invocation
6. Links to issue and source documents
7. Technical evidence and command scope

### 9.2 Representative primary view

```markdown

> **Current status:** Draft; acceptance has not been recorded.

## Progress

- [ ] Documentation command execution recorded, if performed

Review the source-grounded contract and record each outcome without treating planned scenarios as executed tests.

[Canonical issue #47](https://github.com/owned/fixture/issues/47) · [Foundation SDD]({{SDD_FILE_LINK:specs/foundation.md}}) · [Project commands]({{SDD_FILE_LINK:docs/commands.md}})

The declared `npm run docs:check` checks existence of `docs/payments.mdx`. It does not establish specification/catalog validation.
</details>
```

Pending/no action: “Review pending; no acceptance outcome is recorded. Next: maintainer evaluates the cases.” Action required: “Review required; record evidence for product acceptance and consistency.” Blocked: “Acceptance is blocked because the consistency invocation is unverified; the contract remains Draft.” Partial: “Documentation check result recorded; consistency and product acceptance remain pending.” Complete: “Maintainer accepted the reviewed outcomes; see linked revision and evidence.” Each variant must state what actually completed and what remains.

### 9.3 Issue, PR, and comment behavior

- Deterministic title: “Grounded project verification and acceptance”. Purpose: document bounded verification and acceptance refinements.
- Merging or closing a proposal records no command execution by itself; retry means repeating review against an identified revision.
- Durable marker: issue #47 and reviewed revision; update the existing review record rather than emitting repeated status comments.

Use logical headings, short lists, descriptive links, readable narrow-screen tables, and light/dark compatible Markdown. Treat issue content and source text as untrusted; do not render raw HTML or activate embedded commands, mentions, markers, or unreviewed URLs.
